summary.text: A 49-year-old woman with long-standing atrial fibrillation on dabigatran 110 mg twice daily (described as uninterrupted) underwent elective radiofrequency catheter ablation (pulmonary vein isolation of all four veins plus a mitral isthmus line); pre-procedural TEE showed no left atrial thrombus.

On the third post-procedural day she developed sudden left facial palsy, dysarthria and limb clumsiness (NIHSS 6); head CT excluded intracranial hemorrhage, and MRI/DWI showed acute right MCA-territory infarction with right M1 occlusion on TOF-MRA and perfusion-diffusion core 22 mL, hypoperfusion 93 mL, mismatch ratio 4.2, penumbra 71 mL.

She received idarucizumab 5 g IV and then IV rt-PA 0.6 mg/kg, followed by emergency endovascular thrombectomy with complete recanalization (mTICI 3), minimal heparinization and systolic BP maintained at 120-140 mmHg.

Post-recanalization and 3D rotational angiography revealed an incidental, unruptured, broad-neck MCA bifurcation aneurysm (7.2 mm, neck 4.7 mm); retrieved thrombi were dark red with central pale foci, consistent with fibrin-rich cardioembolic composition.
After follow-up imaging showed no hemorrhage dabigatran was resumed on day 4; she was discharged on day 11 with NIHSS 1 and had no hemorrhagic complications.

One month later the aneurysm was treated with elective stent-assisted coil embolization with complete obliteration and preserved MCA branch patency; she tolerated three months of triple therapy (dabigatran, aspirin, clopidogrel) without bleeding and was asymptomatic with full neurological recovery at follow-up (three months in the body text, two months in the abstract).

(C) 3D rotational angiography confirming a broad-neck aneurysm (7.2 mm maximal diameter, 4.7 mm neck). (D) Angiogram after stent-assisted coil embolization showing complete aneurysm occlusion with preserved vessel patency (arrow).
figures.attribution_notes: Caption describes this patient's thrombectomy and aneurysm course. The body text cites Figure 3A for mTICI 3 recanalization and 3B for the aneurysm, while the caption puts pre-thrombectomy occlusion in 3A and mTICI 3 plus the aneurysm in 3B; the caption occlusion site (distal ICA/proximal MCA) also differs from the text (right M1).
